subject: EU backup sweep / KMS key deletion — audit window & propagation SLA
content:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@alderfin.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Subject: Question: how do backups get removed after an EU data erase request?

Hi Sean,

We're preparing for a GDPR-compliant data erasure request from one of our EU customers and want to understand how Redwood handles backup deletion in the EU region. Specifically:

- If we request erasure for a customer dataset, how long until backups in EU regions are actually expunged?
- If customer used Redwood-managed KMS keys, does key deletion factor into the timeline or do you keep snapshots until the key is gone?
- We need auditor evidence showing deletion windows and logs — what's your standard artefact set and how quickly can you produce it?

Thanks,
Liam
Alder Financial — InfoSec

---
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@alderfin.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question: how do backups get removed after an EU data erase request?

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers first, then I’ll pull in precise evidence/examples.

1) Typical timeline (EU region, Redwood-managed flow):
   - Deletion request acknowledged -> we mark live records for erasure immediately.
   - Associated snapshots receive a tombstone marker during the next metadata sweep (sweeps run every 24 hours).
   - Tombstoned snapshots are eligible for expunge; expunge jobs run in batches every 6 hours.
   - Cross-region replication of tombstone markers is async; in EU pairs we see propagation within ~1–4 hours after tombstone metadata is written.
   - Final cryptographic expunge (removal of stored object data) completes within 72 hours of tombstone in normal cases, but can extend to 5–7 days under high load or pending legal holds.

2) KMS impact:
   - For Redwood-managed keys: key-scheduling is separate. We do not automatically delete CMKs on a data-erasure event. If you request key destruction, AWS/GCP KMS provides a configurable waiting window (commonly 7–30 days) which will affect the ability to cryptographically make backups unrecoverable.
   - For customer-managed keys (CMKs you control): you remain able to revoke access immediately; Redwood respects your KMS controls and will report key state in evidence artifacts.

3) Evidence for auditors:
   - We can provide: timestamped metadata change logs showing tombstone write, expunge job run logs (job id + start/end + items processed), S3/GCS object deletion events (where applicable), and a short summary CSV that maps customer object ids to deletion events.

I’ll attach a sample CSV and an audit evidence template. Karthik, can you add the low-level notes about tombstone retention ranges and legal-hold overrides?

—Sean

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@alderfin.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:38:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question: how do backups get removed after an EU data erase request?

Adding technical details:

- Metadata model: we use a two-phase lifecycle for backups — tombstone (soft-delete) and expunge (hard-delete). Tombstone records are retained for a configurable tombstone window (standard 48–168 hours depending on customer SLA).
- Expunge mechanics: expunge workers read tombstone indexes; to reduce customer impact we only hard-delete immutable object segments after verifying no outstanding replication or restore pointers exist. That verification is local to the EU shard and also checks the cross-region replication ledger to avoid race conditions.
- Replication & visibility: tombstone propagation is performed via an append-only replication log. Entries are pushed to peers; peers apply tombstones in sequence. In heavy traffic windows the apply lag can be up to ~4 hours but we have operational alerts when lag exceeds 6 hours.
- Key handling nuance: if a Redwood-managed KMS key is scheduled for destruction, object re-encryption is not performed — the system marks objects as crypto-unrecoverable only after the KMS deletion finalizes. If you need an auditable immediate cryptographic unrecoverability, the recommended path is to request a KMS-scheduled-delete and provide Redwood the envelope id so we can correlate.
- Legal holds & audit: placing a legal hold flips a retention flag that prevents tombstone->expunge transitions. Legal holds are visible in the metadata and will appear in evidence exports.

Attached are two things: a small sample expunge run log (CSV) and an internal audit artefact template (PDF).

-Karthik

Attachments: expunge-run-log-sample.csv (attached), aegis_audit_evidence_template.pdf (attached)

2) Alder to indicate willingness to schedule Redwood-managed KMS key deletion (Alder) — include desired pending window (7/14/30 days).
3) Redwood to queue a priority expunge run once tombstone is written and provide a consolidated audit bundle (Redwood) — target: deliver within 48 hours of finalizer (we will aim for 24h where operationally possible).

Please note: expedited handling requires a signed amendment because it changes standard SLA behavior and might impact neighboring tenants during heavy DR activity.
